params.value: 19,432,294,256 BF16 params (HF safetensors count, includes the vision tower). Card: about 19B total, about 3B active, plus a 0.4B MTP layer. Pruned from Qwen3.6-35B-A3B: config.json is identical to Qwen3.6-35B-A3B except num_experts 128 vs 256 (plus pad_token_id, router_aux_loss_coef 0.0, use_cache), so the routed experts per layer were cut in half. Vendor reply in GGUF discussion #2 (2026-11-02): 'the model was pruned from the base model, though the pruning method was not REAP'. The method is not disclosed. Per-token read estimate from config: about 1.13B expert + about 1.8B attention/GDN + 0.51B lm_head = about 3.4B.

architecture.value: Qwen3_5MoeForConditionalGeneration (model_type qwen3_5_moe), the same as Qwen3.6-35B-A3B. 40 layers, full_attention_interval 4: 10 full-attention layers (16 Q heads, 2 KV heads, head_dim 256, output gate, partial rotary 0.25, rope_theta 1e7, mrope) and 30 Gated DeltaNet linear-attention layers (16 key heads x128, 32 value heads x128, conv kernel 4, SSM state float32). Hidden 2048. MoE: 128 routed experts (intermediate 512) + 1 shared (512), 8 routed per token. Vocab 248,320, untied embeddings. 1 MTP layer. Vision tower 27 layers, hidden 1152.

context_length.value: max_position_embeddings 262,144; YaRN factor 4 to about 1M per the card; the card recommends keeping at least 128K for thinking. On this GPU: about 128k (llama.cpp Q4_K_M, f16 KV) or 256k (q8_0 KV); vLLM NVFP4 --language-model-only about 128k BF16 KV / 257k FP8 KV.

modalities.value: Image and video input + text output (image-text-to-text, 'natively multimodal'). Text-only path: vLLM --language-model-only (skips the BF16 vision tower, about 0.84 GiB); llama.cpp: pass --no-mmproj with -hf so mmproj-Groot-19B-A3B-261023-BF16.gguf (0.84 GiB) is not auto-loaded.

thinking.how_to_toggle: Thinking is on by default: the template appends '<think>\n'; enable_thinking=false appends an empty think block. The card says there are no /think or /nothink soft switches. vLLM: per request chat_template_kwargs {"enable_thinking": false}; server default --default-chat-template-kwargs '{"enable_thinking":false}' (present at v0.33.0); --reasoning-parser qwen3 (trace in 'reasoning'). llama.cpp b12407: --chat-template-kwargs '{"enable_thinking":false}' or --reasoning off as the server default, with per-request chat_template_kwargs; --reasoning-budget N. Ollama: only the community upload exists, and it lists only the vision capability, so the 'think' toggle is unverified. TEMPLATE DISCREPANCY: chat_template.jinja (embedded in the official GGUF) re-emits <think> for every past assistant turn and ignores preserve_thinking; the tokenizer_config.json template (used by bartowski) drops past reasoning unless preserve_thinking=true, as the card describes.

vllm.arch_supported: Yes. v0.33.0 registry.py line 205 Qwen3_5MoeForCausalLM, lines 618-620 Qwen3_5MoeForConditionalGeneration, line 740 Qwen3_5MoeMTP. Card asks for vLLM >= 0.19.1.
vllm.kv_math: Budget 16303 MiB x 0.92 = 14999 MiB = 14.65 GiB. NVFP4 shards 11.78 GiB incl. BF16 vision tower (estimated 0.84 GiB from the mmproj). KV per token = 2 x 10 full layers x 2 KV heads x 256 x 2 B = 20,480 B BF16, 10,240 B FP8. GDN state per sequence = 30 x (32x128x128x4 + 8192x3x2) B = 0.06 GiB. (a) With vision: 14.65-11.78-1.2 = 1.67, minus 0.06 = 1.61 GiB -> 84.5k BF16 / 169k FP8. (b) --language-model-only: 14.65-10.94-1.2 = 2.51, minus 0.06 = 2.45 GiB -> 128.5k BF16 / 257k FP8 (cap 262,144). (c) LM-only + MTP (0.82 GiB): 1.63 GiB -> 85k BF16 / 171k FP8.
vllm.quant_on_sm120: Experts are NVFP4 weight-only (input_activations null), so compressed_tensors_moe.py builds CompressedTensorsW4A4Nvfp4MoEMethod(use_a16=True). oracle/nvfp4.py tries FlashInfer backends, then VLLM_CUTLASS, then MARLIN; Humming is prioritized only on cc 90, so on sm_120 the MoE runs on MARLIN W4A16 (inferred; matches the kernels logged in #54331). This avoids the W4A4 JIT RAM spike #46268. Attention/GDN projections are FP8 W8A8 static per-tensor. FP8 KV needs --attention-backend TRITON_ATTN (baseline #61239).
vllm.min_version: 0.19.1 per the card; present at v0.33.0
vllm.serve_command: docker run --rm --gpus all --ipc=host --memory 24g -p 127.0.0.1:8000:8000 -v $HOME/.cache/huggingface:/root/.cache/huggingface vllm/vllm-openai:v0.33.0 GrootTeam/Groot-19B-A3B-261023-NVFP4 --served-model-name groot-19b-a3b --language-model-only --max-model-len 131072 --gpu-memory-utilization 0.92 --kv-cache-dtype fp8 --attention-backend TRITON_ATTN --max-num-seqs 2 --enable-auto-tool-choice --tool-call-parser qwen3_coder --reasoning-parser qwen3 --default-chat-template-kwargs '{"enable_thinking":false}'
vllm.known_issues: #54331 OPEN: sm_120 hybrid-GDN NVFP4 (qwen3_5_moe, MARLIN NvFp4 MoE, also nvidia/Qwen3.6-35B-A3B-NVFP4) crashes under sustained concurrent load with CUDA graphs on; only enforce_eager survived. Same arch and kernel path, so fall back to --enforce-eager if it crashes. MTP costs 0.82 GiB and drops the KV pool to about 85k BF16. The card's serve commands use the wrong repo id 'Groot/...'.

speed_notes: Inferred: about 3.4B params read per token x about 0.61 B/param (Q4_K_M) = about 2.1 GB/token, so 896 GB/s gives a ceiling of about 430 tok/s; expect about 150-250 tok/s decode at short context, all in VRAM (much faster than Qwen3.6-35B-A3B with --n-cpu-moe 21). Third-party measured on RTX PRO 6000 (1792 GB/s), vLLM NVFP4+MTP: 379 tok/s decode, 303 tok/s at 120k context, prefill 27k tok/s at 32k (Blackwall). One user reported half the speed of Qwen3.6-35B Q4_K_M (GGUF discussion #3, unexplained). Not measured on this machine.

opencode_fit.caveats: A strong challenger to pick #1 (Qwen3.6-35B-A3B): it fits fully in 16 GB at 128k and has the same tool format and parsers. Measure it before promoting it. (1) Anonymous publisher (user account, unverified org, team question unanswered), no LICENSE file, undisclosed pruning method and data. (2) All agentic scores are self-reported; on the vendor's own chart it loses to Qwen3.6 on SWE-bench Verified (31.66 vs 36.27) and ties on BFCL v4; the only third-party eval is a single Blackwall run without Qwen3.6. (3) Community reports: knowledge loss and alleged data shaping (GGUF discussion #3), only English and Chinese output, verbatim path text altered (discussion #5), which is risky for a coding agent. (4) chat_template.jinja differs from the tokenizer_config template; llama.cpp #30357/#30118 likely apply. (5) The vLLM NVFP4 path shares #54331. Run an OpenCode A/B against Qwen3.6-35B-A3B, thinking on and off.
